flashcard_questions.a: The chance that something will go wrong, losing time or money.
Someone prepared to take a risk hoping for a reward by running a business.

flashcard_questions.q: What is financial loss for a business?
flashcard_questions.a: When costs are higher than income, so the owner loses money.

flashcard_questions.q: What does lack of security mean for an entrepreneur?
flashcard_questions.a: There is no guaranteed wage and no safety net if the business struggles.

flashcard_questions.q: What proportion of small businesses fail in their first year?
What proportion of small businesses fail within five years?
Which fashion brand went bust in March 2024 after debts piled up?
What number of jobs was put at risk when Claire's UK went into administration?
Which video rental business failed by not moving to streaming quickly enough?
What fine did Alton Towers receive after the Smiler crash?
Why did KFC close hundreds of UK branches in 2018?
flashcard_questions.a: Its new delivery supplier struggled with the volume.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the financial loss when stock bought for £800 sells for only £600?
How much do cyber attacks cost UK small firms each year?
What reward does independence give an entrepreneur?
flashcard_questions.a: The freedom to make their own decisions without answering to a boss.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the drawback of the profit reward for an entrepreneur?
flashcard_questions.a: Some profit must be reinvested as equipment wears out.

notes: 15 cards: 4 term→definition (risk, entrepreneur, financial loss, lack of security), 2 failure-rate statistics, 5 concept→named example (Ted Baker, Claire's 2,150 jobs, Blockbuster, Alton Towers £5m, KFC 2018), 1 one-step calculation on the £800/£600 stock example, 1 cyber-cost figure, 2 reward cards. Avoided the Wilko and Body Shop questions because the old deck already asked those two almost word for word.
